images.title: Where Robby and Deeku both land
images.purpose: Show the jumps of 2 and the jumps of 5 from 0 on one number line, so the stones both land on, 10, 20 and 30, are the common multiples of 2 and 5.
images.composition: One number line from 0 to 30 with small teal arcs for jumps of 2, large amber arcs for jumps of 5, three purple boxes on 10, 20 and 30, a legend and a caption.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A horizontal number line, dark #2B2B2B, 5 px thick, at y 520 from x 100 to x 1356 with an arrowhead at the right end. 31 vertical ticks, one at every whole number from 0 to 30, 20 px tall (y 510 to 530), at x = 128 + 40 times the number, so 0 is at x 128, 10 at x 528, 20 at x 928 and 30 at x 1328. Under every tick its number, dark #1F2937 (28 px, bold), centred at y 575: all 31 numbers 0 to 30. ROBBY'S JUMPS (teal #0072B2): exactly 15 arcs above the line, 4 px thick, each from one even number to the next (from 0 to 2, 2 to 4, and so on to 28 to 30), each 80 px wide and 50 px high, with a teal dot (12 px) on the line at each landing 2, 4, ..., 30 (15 dots). DEEKU'S JUMPS (amber #E69F00): exactly 6 arcs above the line and above the teal arcs, 5 px thick, each from one multiple of 5 to the next (0 to 5, 5 to 10, and so on to 25 to 30), each 200 px wide and 140 px high, with an amber dot (16 px) on the line at each landing 5, 10, ..., 30 (6 dots). At 10, 20 and 30 the amber dot has the smaller teal dot inside it. Exactly 3 reddish purple #CC79A7 rectangles, 6 px outline, no fill, 80 by 50 px, around the numbers 10, 20 and 30 (centres x 528, 928 and 1328, y 575). Top left, a legend: at x 150 and y 110 a teal arc sample and a small flat rabbit icon (70 px tall) with the text Robby jumps 2; at x 150 and y 190 an amber arc sample and a small flat deer icon (90 px tall) with the text Deeku jumps 5 (36 px, dark). At the bottom, centred at x 728 and y 720, the text Both land on 10, 20 and 30 in bold dark #1F2937 (52 px). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The numbers both jumpers land on, 10, 20 and 30, are the common multiples of 2 and 5, and 10 is the first.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 30 with jumps of 2 in teal and jumps of 5 in amber, and 10, 20 and 30 boxed where both land.
images.context: Concept image for Common Multiples. It follows the idea of the rabbit and frog number lines in your maths book (two jumpers, the numbers both touch) and uses this concept's own example, jumps of 2 and 5.
images.teaching_notes: Follow each jumper along the line and say the numbers it lands on, then look for the stones with both marks. The slip to watch is counting only the product 2 × 5 and stopping.

image_decisions.why: The two sets of jumps on one number line show the numbers both jumpers touch, which is the whole meaning of common multiples.
